data.title: Slide Insurance Holdings (NASDAQ:SLDE) Ticks All The Boxes When It Comes To Earnings Growth
data.description:
Investors are often guided by the idea of discovering 'the next big thing', even if that means buying 'story stocks' without any revenue, let alone profit. Sometimes these stories can cloud the minds of investors, leading them to invest with their emotions rather than on the merit of good company fundamentals. Loss making companies can act like a sponge for capital - so investors should be cautious that they're not throwing good money after bad.

In contrast to all that, many investors prefer to focus on companies like Slide Insurance Holdings (NASDAQ:SLDE), which has not only revenues, but also profits. Now this is not to say that the company presents the best investment opportunity around, but profitability is a key component to success in business.

Slide Insurance Holdings' Improving Profits

Over the last three years, Slide Insurance Holdings has grown earnings per share (EPS) at as impressive rate from a relatively low point, resulting in a three year percentage growth rate that isn't particularly indicative of expected future performance. As a result, we'll zoom in on growth over the last year, instead. In previous twelve months, Slide Insurance Holdings' EPS has risen from US$4.33 to US$4.76. That's a fair increase of 9.9%. EPS has grown further thank to a share buyback. A great indicator of a healthy balance sheet.

It's often helpful to take a look at earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margins, as well as revenue growth, to get another take on the quality of the company's growth. Slide Insurance Holdings shareholders can take confidence from the fact that EBIT margins are up from 36% to 53%, and revenue is growing. Both of which are great metrics to check off for potential growth.

Are Slide Insurance Holdings Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

Many consider high insider ownership to be a strong sign of alignment between the leaders of a company and the ordinary shareholders. So as you can imagine, the fact that Slide Insurance Holdings insiders own a significant number of shares certainly is appealing. Owning 41% of the company, insiders have plenty riding on the performance of the the share price. This should be a welcoming sign for investors because it suggests that the people making the decisions are also impacted by their choices. US$1.2b That level of investment from insiders is nothing to sneeze at.

It means a lot to see insiders invested in the business, but shareholders may be wondering if remuneration policies are in their best interest. Our quick analysis into CEO remuneration would seem to indicate they are. Our analysis has discovered that the median total compensation for the CEOs of companies like Slide Insurance Holdings with market caps between US$2.0b and US$6.4b is about US$7.0m.

Slide Insurance Holdings' CEO took home a total compensation package worth US$4.0m in the year leading up to December 2025. That comes in below the average for similar sized companies and seems pretty reasonable. While the level of CEO compensation shouldn't be the biggest factor in how the company is viewed, modest remuneration is a positive, because it suggests that the board keeps shareholder interests in mind. It can also be a sign of a culture of integrity, in a broader sense.

Does Slide Insurance Holdings Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?

As previously touched on, Slide Insurance Holdings is a growing business, which is encouraging. The fact that EPS is growing is a genuine positive for Slide Insurance Holdings, but the pleasant picture gets better than that. With a meaningful level of insider ownership, and reasonable CEO pay, a reasonable mind might conclude that this is one stock worth watching. You should always think about risks though. Higher yields pull income seekers back toward bonds, yet they also shine a spotlight on large-cap value and high-dividend stocks that might still offer attractive cash returns. Ameren (AEE)

Overview: Ameren is a regulated utility group supplying electricity and natural gas to homes, businesses, and industry across Missouri and Illinois, aligning with income-focused value investors seeking large-cap U.S. dividend payers.

Operations: Ameren generates about US$4.6b from Ameren Missouri, US$2.5b from Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution, US$1.0b from Ameren Illinois Natural Gas, and US$0.9b from Ameren Transmission, all within the US$8.4b U.S. market.

Market Cap: US$29.0b

Public Storage (PSA)

Public Storage slots neatly into this value and income screen because its self-storage platform converts everyday space constraints into relatively steady rent checks for shareholders.

"Urban densification and the continued shrinkage of residential living space in major metro markets are driving demand for self-storage, benefiting Public Storage's occupancy rates and supporting revenue, as evidenced by leasing activity and stabilization trends in high-density regions such as the West Coast."

data.title: How Quality Push At Humana (HUM) Has Changed Its Investment Story
data.description:
• Humana's board previously approved a cash dividend of $0.885 per share, scheduled for payment on November 27, 2026 to stockholders of record on October 30, 2026.
  • The payout lands while Humana works to offset expected 2026 profit pressure from weak Medicare Advantage Star Ratings through pharmacy integration and the use of quality vendors such as Counterpart Health.
  • We will examine how Humana's investment narrative is influenced by its quality initiatives as it maintains a cash dividend of $0.885 per share.

Scan how Humana’s dividend story compares with other income-focused opportunities by reviewing our curated list of 6 dividend fortresses in the current market.

Humana Investment Narrative Recap

To own Humana, you need to be comfortable with a health insurer that leans heavily on Medicare Advantage, value based care through CenterWell, and tight cost control. The immediate swing factor is how well Humana can blunt the expected US$3.5b profit hit tied to weak 2026 Star Ratings through pharmacy integration and quality programs.

The dividend affirmation at US$0.885 per share is, on its own, not a major swing item for the thesis. The bigger near term risk remains pressure on medical cost trends and any further disruption from coding, reimbursement or litigation around Star Ratings that could strain already thin 0.9% net margins.

The most relevant piece of context for this dividend decision is Humana’s push into integrated specialty pharmacy and lower drug cost models. Management is tying member engagement, medication adherence and coordinated pharmacy care together, which aims to support more stable medical cost ratios and help offset quality related funding pressure.

Counterpart Health’s role in closing HEDIS gaps and supporting better clinical quality for PPO members fits directly into that effort. Execution on these quality and pharmacy initiatives will influence whether Humana can meaningfully reduce the impact of weaker 2026 Star Ratings on earnings volatility, while maintaining enough cash flow flexibility to keep funding dividends and growth projects.

Humana Earnings Path Behind the Dividend

Humana's long term story that sits behind a steady US$0.885 per share dividend is built on analysts expecting the business to compound revenue at 8.5% per year and expand margins from 0.9% to 1.8% over the next three years. The earnings bridge is sizeable in dollar terms. Consensus points to net income rising from US$1.3b today to US$3.4b by 2029, with some analysts seeing as much as US$4.3b and others closer to US$2.6b, which shows how sensitive the outcome is to execution on quality, pharmacy integration and Stars recovery.

On those projections, analysts see Humana generating US$186.1b of revenue and US$3.4b of earnings by 2029. That profile implies 8.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$2.1b from current earnings of US$1.3b.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view leans on Humana’s Medicare Advantage and CenterWell expansion as a powerful long term tailwind. The most optimistic analysts were penciling in revenue of US$207.8b and earnings of US$4.2b by 2029 before this dividend news.
